title: 카페 · 커피
intro: '카페'는 자주 가는 카페 묘사 → 카페에서 하는 일(루틴) → 기억에 남는 경험 → 예전과 지금의 카페 이용 비교 순서로 자주 출제됩니다. 페르소나는 혼자 사는 4년차 직장인으로, 주말이면 집에서 걸어서 5분 거리의 작은 동네 카페에서 아이스 아메리카노를 마시며 책을 읽고, 퇴근 후엔 친구나 동료 Minji와 카페에서 수다를 떱니다. '동네 카페 하나 + 주말 독서 + 대학 때는 시험공부 장소였다'는 설정 하나로 네 문제를 모두 연결하세요.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장(Oh, cafes? Sure, I'd love to talk about that.) → 기본 정보(어느 카페·어디·얼마나 자주) → 세부(인테리어·메뉴·하는 일) → 느낌·이유(바쁜 한 주 뒤의 휴식) → 마무리 문장(Yeah, that's my favorite cafe.)
카페는 항상 '아파트에서 걸어서 5분, 지하철역 근처의 작고 조용한 동네 카페' 하나로 고정하세요. 큰 창문, 나무 테이블, 잔잔한 음악, 커피 향 같은 쉬운 묘사 3~4개면 충분합니다.
루틴은 도착 → 주문(iced Americano) → 창가 자리 → 책 읽기·휴대폰 → 두세 시간 후 귀가 순서로 시간 흐름을 따라가면 막히지 않습니다.
비교 질문은 '대학 때는 친구들과 시험공부하러 밤늦게까지 → 지금은 주말에 혼자 쉬러, 가끔 금요일 재택근무 날 노트북 작업' 구도로 답하세요.

expressions.en: Oh, cafes? Sure, I'd love to talk about that.
expressions.note: 주제 시작 문장: 질문 키워드를 한 번 되묻고 시작

expressions.en: There's a small cafe about five minutes from my apartment.
expressions.ko: 우리 아파트에서 5분 정도 거리에 작은 카페가 있어요.
expressions.note: There's + 장소 + 거리: 기본 정보 문장

expressions.en: I go there almost every weekend.
I always order an iced Americano.
expressions.note: an iced Americano: 관사 an + iced

expressions.en: It has big windows and wooden tables.
I like to sit by the window.
I usually read a book there for a couple of hours.
expressions.ko: 보통 거기서 두어 시간 책을 읽어요.
expressions.note: a couple of hours: 두세 시간

expressions.en: It's a great place to relax after a busy week.
expressions.ko: 바쁜 한 주를 보내고 쉬기에 좋은 곳이에요.

expressions.en: The coffee smells amazing as soon as you walk in.
It's quiet enough to read, but it doesn't feel empty.
expressions.ko: 책 읽기에 충분히 조용하지만 썰렁한 느낌은 아니에요.

expressions.en: Back in college, I used to study there until late at night.
expressions.ko: 대학 때는 거기서 밤늦게까지 공부하곤 했어요.
expressions.note: used to + 동사: 과거의 습관 (비교 질문)

expressions.en: These days, I go to cafes to rest, not to study.
expressions.ko: 요즘은 공부하러가 아니라 쉬러 카페에 가요.
expressions.note: to A, not to B: 목적 대비

expressions.en: We ended up talking for three hours.
The barista knows my order by heart, which makes me feel like a regular.
expressions.ko: 바리스타가 제 주문을 외우고 있어서 단골이 된 기분이에요.
expressions.note: by heart: 외워서 / , which: 앞 문장 전체 수식

expressions.en: So yeah, that's pretty much why that little cafe means so much to me.
expressions.ko: 그래서 네, 그게 그 작은 카페가 제게 그렇게 소중한 이유예요.
expressions.note: 마무리 문장: So yeah, that's pretty much why ~

questions.en: You indicated in the survey that you like going to cafes. Tell me about a cafe you often go to. Where is it, and what does it look like?
questions.ko: 설문에서 카페 가는 걸 좋아한다고 하셨네요. 자주 가는 카페에 대해 말해 주세요. 어디에 있고, 어떻게 생겼나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 위치(아파트에서 걸어서 5분, 지하철역 근처) → 생김새(큰 창문, 나무 테이블, 식물) → 분위기·좋아하는 이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
입구 → 카운터 → 자리 순서로 '들어가는 길'을 따라 묘사하면 막히지 않아요
냄새·소리(coffee smell, soft music) 한 문장을 넣으면 IH 이상으로 들려요

answers.IM3: Oh, cafes? Sure, let me tell you about my favorite cafe. There's a small cafe about five minutes from my apartment. It's near the subway station. It's not very big, but it's really cozy. It has big windows and wooden tables. There are some plants by the windows, too. They usually play soft music, so it's quiet. I like to sit by the window and read a book. I go there almost every weekend. Yeah, that's my favorite cafe.
answers.IH: Oh, cafes? Sure, I'd love to talk about that. There's a small cafe I go to almost every weekend. It's only about a five-minute walk from my apartment, right next to the subway station. From the outside, it looks pretty simple, but inside it's really cozy. When you walk in, the coffee smells amazing. The counter is on the left, and there are about eight wooden tables. The best part is the big windows. A lot of sunlight comes in, and there are small green plants on the window sills. They always play soft jazz or acoustic music, so it's quiet enough to read, but it doesn't feel empty. My favorite seat is the one by the window, because I can watch people walking by. After a busy week at work, it's the perfect place to relax. Yeah, that's my favorite cafe in my neighborhood.
answers.AL: Oh, cafes? Sure, I'd love to talk about that, because I'm kind of a cafe person. There's a small cafe I go to almost every weekend, and it's only about a five-minute walk from my apartment, right by the subway station. Honestly, it's one of the reasons I like my neighborhood so much. From the outside, it doesn't look like much, just a white wall and a small wooden sign, but inside it's super cozy. As soon as you open the door, you can smell the coffee beans they roast themselves. The counter is on the left, and there are maybe eight or nine wooden tables with comfy chairs. What I love the most are the huge windows. On sunny afternoons, the whole place is filled with warm light, and there are little plants lined up on the window sills. They always play soft acoustic music, so it's calm enough to read, but there's still a nice buzz of people chatting. I've been going there for almost three years now, so the barista knows my order by heart, which makes me feel like a regular. So yeah, that's pretty much why that little cafe means so much to me.

questions.en: Why do you go to cafes, and what do you usually do there? Tell me about what you typically do from the moment you arrive until you leave.
questions.ko: 왜 카페에 가고, 거기서 주로 무엇을 하나요? 도착해서 나올 때까지 보통 하는 일을 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 왜(바쁜 한 주 뒤 혼자 쉬는 시간) → 도착·주문(아이스 아메리카노) → 자리·하는 일(책, 휴대폰) → 나오기 → 마무리 문장
When I get there, First, Then, After a couple of hours 같은 순서 표현을 쓰세요
혼자 갈 때(주말 독서)와 친구와 갈 때(퇴근 후 수다)를 짧게 나눠 말하면 IH 이상 답변이 돼요

answers.IM3: Sure, let me tell you about it. I go to cafes because I want to relax after a busy week. My weekdays are pretty busy because I have a lot of meetings. So on Saturday afternoon, I go to a small cafe near my apartment. When I get there, I order an iced Americano. Then I sit by the window. I usually read a book for a couple of hours. Sometimes I just look at my phone. After that, I walk back home. Yeah, that's what I usually do at cafes.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about that. I mainly go to cafes to take a break from my busy life. I work at an IT company, and my weekdays are full of meetings and reports, so on weekends I really need some quiet time. Usually on Saturday afternoon, I walk to a small cafe near my apartment. When I get there, I order an iced Americano, even in winter, and sometimes a piece of cheesecake. Then I find a seat by the window. First, I check my phone for a few minutes, and then I put it away and read a book. These days, I'm reading a mystery novel. I usually stay for about two or three hours. Sometimes on weekday evenings, I go to cafes with my friends instead, and we just chat about work and life. After that, I walk home feeling really calm. So yeah, that's my usual cafe routine.
answers.AL: Sure, I'd love to talk about that. To be honest, cafes are kind of my escape from the busy office life. I work on the marketing team at an IT company, and my weekdays are packed with meetings, reports, and messages, so by the weekend, I really need some time just for myself. Most Saturday afternoons, I take a short walk to a little cafe near my apartment. The moment I walk in, the barista usually says, 'Iced Americano, right?' because I order the same thing every single time, even in the middle of winter. If I'm in a good mood, I treat myself to a slice of cheesecake, too. Then I grab my favorite seat by the window. For the first few minutes, I scroll through my phone, but then I make myself put it away and open a book. Right now I'm into mystery novels, and I can easily lose track of time. I usually end up staying for two or three hours. On some weekday evenings, though, it's a totally different vibe, because I meet my friends at a cafe and we chat about work and life until they close. Either way, I always leave feeling recharged. So yeah, that's pretty much my cafe routine.

questions.en: Tell me about a memorable experience you had at a cafe. What happened, who were you with, and why was it so memorable?
questions.ko: 카페에서 있었던 기억에 남는 경험을 말해 주세요. 무슨 일이 있었고, 누구와 함께였으며, 왜 그렇게 기억에 남나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제·누구와(작년 겨울, 동료 Minji) → 무슨 일(큰 캠페인 끝난 날 축하 → 갑자기 폭설) → 결과(세 시간 수다, 더 친해짐) → 느낌 → 마무리 문장
과거 시제를 끝까지 유지하고, 'Suddenly', 'In the end' 같은 연결어로 이야기의 전환점을 표시하세요
마지막에 '그 이후로 ~' 한 문장으로 지금과 연결하면 자연스럽게 마무리돼요

answers.IM3: Oh, let me think. I remember one day last winter. I went to a cafe with my coworker Minji. We finished a big project that day, so we wanted to celebrate. We ordered hot chocolate and cake. Then suddenly, it started to snow a lot. We couldn't go home, so we stayed at the cafe. We talked about many things for three hours. It was really fun. After that day, we became much closer. Yeah, that's my most memorable cafe experience.
answers.IH: Oh, I have a good one. Let me think. It was last winter, on a Friday evening. That day, my team finally finished a big SNS campaign that we worked on for two months. My coworker Minji and I were so relieved, so we went to a cafe near our office to celebrate. We ordered hot chocolate and a big piece of strawberry cake. While we were eating, it suddenly started to snow really hard. Within thirty minutes, the streets were completely white, and the subway was super crowded. So we just decided to stay at the cafe. We ended up talking for three hours about our first year at work, our families, and our dreams. I realized we had so much in common. Since then, Minji has been one of my closest friends, not just a coworker. Yeah, that's why that cafe day is so memorable to me.
answers.AL: Oh, I actually have a really good one. Let me think for a second. It was last winter, on a Friday evening right before the holidays. That afternoon, my team had finally wrapped up a huge SNS campaign we'd been working on for almost two months, and honestly, we were all completely exhausted. My coworker Minji, who joined the company the same year as me, suggested we go to a cafe near the office to celebrate. So we ordered two hot chocolates and the biggest slice of strawberry cake they had. While we were laughing about all the crazy things that happened during the project, it suddenly started snowing like crazy. Within half an hour, the whole street was covered in white, and we heard the subway was packed and super slow. Instead of rushing home, we just looked at each other and said, 'Let's stay.' We ended up talking for three whole hours about everything, like our first year at work, our families, and where we want to be in five years. I found out we had way more in common than I'd thought. Ever since that night, Minji has been more like a close friend than a coworker. So yeah, that's pretty much why that snowy cafe night is so special to me.

questions.en: How has the way you use cafes changed over the years? Compare how you used cafes in the past with how you use them now.
questions.ko: 카페를 이용하는 방식이 몇 년 사이 어떻게 변했나요? 예전과 지금의 카페 이용 방식을 비교해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 예전(대전에서 대학 다닐 때, 친구들과 시험공부, 밤늦게까지) → 지금(직장인, 주말에 혼자 쉬러, 가끔 재택근무 날 노트북) → 가장 큰 변화와 이유 → 마무리 문장
Back in college, I used to ~ / These days, I ~ 구조로 과거와 현재를 분명히 나누세요
변화의 이유(학생 → 직장인, 공부 → 휴식)를 한 문장으로 꼭 말해 주세요

answers.IM3: Oh, it has changed a lot. When I was a college student, I went to cafes to study. I studied with my friends for exams. We stayed there until late at night. I drank a lot of coffee to stay awake. Now I work at an IT company. These days, I go to cafes to relax, not to study. I go on weekends and read a book. I feel much more relaxed now. Yeah, that's how my cafe life has changed.
answers.IH: Oh, it has changed a lot over the years. Back in college, I used to go to cafes almost every day, but mostly to study. During exam periods, my friends and I would sit in a big franchise cafe for hours with our laptops and textbooks. We often stayed there until midnight, and I drank three or four cups of coffee a day just to stay awake. Honestly, it was more stressful than relaxing. These days, it's totally different. I work at an IT company now, so I spend all week at the office. That's why I go to cafes to rest, not to study. On weekends, I go to a small, quiet cafe near my apartment and read a book. Sometimes on Fridays, when I work from home, I take my laptop to a cafe for a change of scenery. I also drink just one coffee a day now. So yeah, that's how my cafe life has changed.
answers.AL: Oh, it has changed a lot, and it kind of shows how my life has changed, too. Back in college, cafes were basically my study room. During exam periods, my friends and I would camp out at a big, noisy franchise cafe with our laptops and piles of textbooks. We'd stay there until they kicked us out at midnight, and I used to drink three or four cups of coffee a day just to keep my eyes open. Looking back, it wasn't relaxing at all. It was more like a place where I felt pressure. These days, it's a completely different story. I've been working at an IT company for four years now, and since I'm stuck in meetings all week, cafes have become the place where I recharge. I much prefer small, quiet cafes now, like the one near my apartment, where I can sit by the window and read for a couple of hours. Every now and then, on Fridays when I work from home, I bring my laptop to a cafe just for a change of scenery, but it still feels pretty laid-back. I also cut down to one coffee a day, which my body definitely thanks me for. So yeah, that's pretty much how my cafe life has changed over the years.

pronunciation.tip: 강세는 뒤 음절 '페이'. '카페'처럼 평평하게 읽지 말고 '캐-페이'로 끝을 올려서
강세는 '카'에. '아메리카노'를 똑같은 박자로 읽지 말고 '어메리카-노우'처럼 카를 길고 세게
강세는 '리'. 첫 음절은 '버'로 약하게, 마지막 '스타'도 짧게 '버리-스터'
'코지'가 아니라 이중모음 '코우'. z는 성대를 울리는 소리로 '코우-지'
